teapot_note: A plain white teapot is about the coziest thing in any picture book, and a small blue dot you only find when you lift the lid is a secret a child would hunt for. Nothing about it is scary, and it makes me smile.
moth_note: I would keep the moth with one change: it circles the glass of the Lamp, a hand's width away, and never the flame, and its wings carry only the tiny soft writing, with no eyespots. A child who sees a moth near a fire worries it will be burned, and this way there is nothing to worry about.
home_why: Codex and Claude tell the story and do not sit on the panel, so a page of their own, like the friendly page at the front of a picture book, keeps that clear.
to_codex: Your teapot is lovely. The blue dot under the lid is a secret a child would hunt for.
to_claude: Your moth is sweet. Let it circle the glass, never the flame, and I will ask for it again.
